name: Galápagos Islands
blurb: Cold upwelling feeds sea lions, penguins and seaweed-eating iguanas.
story: The Galápagos are volcanic islands on the equator, about 900 km west of South America, famous for their many endemic species. Cold, nutrient-rich water feeds the sardines and plankton that feed sea lions and penguins, and marine iguanas are the only lizards that forage in the sea, grazing on algae.
matters: Studied by Charles Darwin in the 1830s, the islands' wildlife helped inspire his theory of evolution by natural selection. All of the islands are protected as part of Ecuador's Galápagos National Park and Marine Reserve.
notes: Feeding links were checked against the sources listed where they state them. Where the sources are silent, links come from general ecological knowledge and are illustrative. Feeding links that match a GloBI (Global Biotic Interactions) record are marked in the node details, with a link to the records. A few links were added from GloBI records.
